summary: Avoid worktree lease processes for reconciliation that only validates or observes existing workspaces

schema.detail: No storage, client schema or code generation changes.

compatibility.detail: Existing workspaces acquire deletion-barrier admission only when the pass renders or starts them, not during validation and observation alone. Observed Git identities survive reclamation between observation and admission; workspace existence and checkout validity are checked again under admission before rendering. A reclaimed workspace is blocked for this pass rather than recreated as a plain directory by rendering. Creation, rendering, runtime initialization and completion publication retain their shared lease, including reused workspaces and detached starts. Rendering remains pass-wide, so restart and full-render passes can still lease every renderable worktree.

downtime.detail: No additional downtime beyond the normal binary restart.

recovery.detail: Binary swap-back requires no data migration.
